Adenocarcinoma originating in the gallbladder, which belongs to the hepatic axis.
In situ carcinoma confined to bladder urothelium; bladder belongs to the renal axis.
Explicitly nonsyndromic CRYAB-related cataract; the broader parent spectrum does not establish muscle or cardiac involvement.
Inherited skin barrier disorder with peeling, xerosis, scaling and dermatitis; no independent immune mechanism or other organ damage established.
Benign neoplasm of vascular endothelial cells; anatomical sites vary, so no additional site-specific axis is assigned.
Systemic Yersinia pseudotuberculosis infection with intestinal and mesenteric inflammation; scarlatiniform rash is transient.
Defining diaphragmatic, limb and skull defects with severe pulmonary hypoplasia; omphalocele is a body-wall defect, not evidence of bowel damage.
Developmental impairment and cataracts define it; renal dysplasia and cleft palate each reported in 1/3. Nonspecific cardiac morphology does not establish damage.
ETFA-related multiple acyl-CoA dehydrogenase deficiency; lipid-storage myopathy and hepatic dysfunction are common (~30%+); cardiac disease varies with severity.
Fibromuscular obstruction of the left ventricular outflow tract below the aortic valve.
Neoplasm occupying the respiratory tract, including upper airways, lungs and pleura.
Cerebrovascular ischemia causing brain tissue infarction; both the cerebral circulation and brain define the disease.
Skeletal dysplasia, myopia and hearing loss define it; upper airway obstruction in 80-99%. Cleft palate in 80-99% omitted because of the four-axis cap.
Immune-mediated cerebral vasculitis with multiple CNS infarctions as a defining feature.
Hypothalamic thirst-regulation dysfunction produces adipsia and hypernatraemia, a defining electrolyte disorder.
Bartonella infection causing characteristic cutaneous vascular proliferation; visceral and bone involvement are variable.
Thymic developmental failure directly causes immunodeficiency; broad endocrine and hematologic ancestors do not establish additional dysfunction.
Congenital unilateral absence or hypoplasia of the radius and associated limb structures.
Developmental delay, intellectual disability and microcephaly define neurologic involvement; cafe-au-lait spots are non-damaging, other organ defects occasional.
GM2 synthase deficiency disrupts ganglioside metabolism and causes spastic neuropathy; scoliosis in 10/15 and amyotrophy in 11/18. Cataracts and urinary findings <30%.
